title: PS21/3: Building operational resilience (SYSC 15A) - abridged demo excerpt
rawText:
Abridged, paraphrased excerpt of the FCA's operational resilience rules (Handbook chapter SYSC 15A, made by PS21/3) prepared for demonstration. Consult the FCA Handbook before relying on it.

SYSC 15A.2 Operational resilience requirements
15A.2.1 R A firm must identify its important business services. An important business service is a service provided by the firm to one or more clients which, if disrupted, could cause intolerable levels of harm to clients or pose a risk to the soundness, stability or resilience of the UK financial system or the orderly operation of financial markets.
15A.2.5 R A firm must, for each of its important business services, set an impact tolerance: the maximum tolerable level of disruption to the service, including the maximum tolerable duration of a disruption.
15A.2.7 R A firm must ensure it is able to remain within its impact tolerance for each important business service in the event of a severe but plausible disruption to its operations.

SYSC 15A.3 Mapping
15A.3.1 R A firm must identify and document the people, processes, technology, facilities and information necessary to deliver each of its important business services, to a level of detail sufficient to identify vulnerabilities and to test its ability to remain within impact tolerances.

SYSC 15A.5 Scenario testing
15A.5.1 R A firm must carry out scenario testing of its ability to remain within its impact tolerance for each of its important business services in the event of a severe but plausible disruption, and must identify an appropriate range of adverse circumstances of varying nature, severity and duration.
15A.5.3 R Where testing identifies that the firm cannot remain within an impact tolerance, the firm must make the necessary changes and record the lessons learned.

SYSC 15A.6 Self-assessment and governance
15A.6.1 R A firm must make and keep an up-to-date written record of its assessment of compliance with these rules, including its important business services, impact tolerances, mapping, scenario testing, lessons learned and remediation. The self-assessment must be approved by the firm's governing body and retained for at least six years.

SYSC 15A.8 Communications
15A.8.1 R A firm must maintain an internal and external communication strategy to act quickly to reduce the anticipated harm caused by operational disruptions, including the provision of timely information to clients, other market participants and the FCA.
15A.8.3 G A firm should notify the FCA of an operational incident that could cause significant harm to consumers or market integrity under SUP 15.3.

Transitional provision: firms had until 31 March 2025 to perform mapping and testing so as to remain within impact tolerances for each important business service.
